mechanism_narrative: A declining federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or the rank correlation between FEDFUNDS trend and returns is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 7.5%, it indicates a weak labor market that suppresses consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months when UNRATE > 7.5%, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals a broad-based weakness in consumer demand, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate revenue expectations are revised downward.
failure_condition: The interaction effect (HOUST and RSAFS both declining) fails to predict negative returns in more than 60% of cases, or the joint signal has a rank IC below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: During manufacturing slowdowns (INDPRO < 95), reduced industrial production leads to lower corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 95, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods with PAYEMS growth, or the rank correlation between PAYEMS trend and returns is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent high inflation (CPIAUCSL YoY change > 3.0) prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY change > 3.0, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in real GDP growth (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a broad economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings forecasts are cut.
failure_condition: The joint signal (GDPC1 and HOUST both declining) fails to predict negative returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction effect has a rank IC below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening regime (FEDFUNDS > 2.0%), the Federal Reserve's policy shift increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 2.0, or the average return in triggered periods is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).
